story_text.value:
This is a free to play, no sign up required domino rally simulator. You design them with the editor, and then run them in the 3D player. The from-behind "Chase" view is best.

My mum helped develop it - she submitted issue reports direct from the app itself (make it possible to bend the domino tracks, make the playback controls disappear while mouse inactive, add like buttons to the showcase, let me change the backdrop, etc) and the Claude Code session running in the cloud watched, fixed them and on my approval, pushed them live.

I've been making a lot of apps in various sessions which share the same repo. One of them https://www.orgiggly.com/david/aurora (an atmospheric musical loop generator) was plundered to generate a unique soundtrack for each rally (seeded by its name) - which is exactly how the orgiggly platform I built is supposed to work - each app created can make contributions to the next one.

story_text.value:
Hey HN readers!

I'm snipedbywifi (https://gitlab.com/snipedbywifi), and i've been working on terminactory. Please try it out if you'd like to play a cozy factory game while waiting for long agent tasks to finish!

The game is a factory game (overused niche, i know xD), but runs in your terminal. Reason i built it? glad you asked: So basically, it started off with me wanting a terminal-native factory game. Me and the modern 5.5 claude models made a base for the game that I liked, and then i went ham adding features / fixing some minor flaws (like adding claude code hooks so you recieve "telegrams" [the agent's responses], so you can review progress directly in-game). (yes, I had heavy AI assistance, disclaimer!!!)

Right now, the game has basic factory features you'd expect from a game like this (build stuff, delete stuff, measure how much you're earning, basic selection tools), along with a few more.. "unexpected" features. This includes a fake in-game browser that has a wiki, fake forums, some fun bits of lore, some more lore, a LOT more lore, and a research graph that shows how many items or how much RP (research points) you'd need to unlock something, and some more QOL features.

If anyone actually has this issue / want of a terminal-based game that runs alongside your agents so you don't doomscroll, do you have any suggestions, or additional ideas I could add?

It's hosted on GitLab, soo, that's one additional thing i'd like to mention

Thanks for reading!! snipedbywifi

(p.s. first HN post lol) (p.s. p.s. there's a lot of hidden lore in the game, so.. lore-divers? you might like it?)

story_text.value:
Hello HN,

I am Ioannis and I would like to introduce Logonomic, a desktop application we made to help us work with LLM CLIs (e.g. codex, claude, opencode etc) in a more organized way. It runs the CLIs already installed, with their existing accounts and configuration and organizes sessions by repository. It is available for Windows and Linux, with a preview for macOS. There is also a mobile companion app, to work remotely (Android and soon iOS too).

We built it originally to assist us in our own work, to address the common case of multiple agents running concurrently in many repositories. It was hard to keep track of what each one is doing and which one needs attention or requires action.

There are many tools by now broadly that broadly target the same problem. This one is a native C++/Qt application with our own terminal emulator. Some of its features:

- An 'overview' mode that shows all running sessions, optionally grouped by repository, each with its status, title and summary that the agents update regularly.

- Agents add a trailer to their commits, enabling to re-open the conversations that produced them.

- Terminals run in their own processes and survive UI crashes.

- A plot that shows line counts over time, by directory or language, where clicking on a sample brings up the corresponding commit in the git log.

- A treemap that shows how the repo's files are organized, with a diff mode that colours changed files, whose diff opens with a double click.

- Token usage and remaining account quotas shown where available, with usage broken down by day and repository.

- Sessions can exchange messages (1:1 or broadcast), may hand tasks to each other or continue other session's work.

The supported CLIs are Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity, Grok Build, Kimi Code and Qwen Code.

The free edition has no time limit and runs up to four terminals. The paid editions have perpetual one-time licences from €150 for 2 seats and include 12 months of feature updates, no terminal limit, GitHub/GitLab CI integrations, as well as an Android companion app (iOS will follow).

The application itself is proprietary. Many of its core components are open source, among them the terminal emulator and the plotting library: https://github.com/Varinomics

This is the first public release, so there will be rough edges, and we would like to hear about them.

story_text.value:
If you already have multiple coding agents(one kind of agent also works though), you should really look into this project! It's a desktop app that brings coding agents working together, with user experience similar to ChatGPT!

One kind of agent is enough for an agent team: all of one kind, or any mix of Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor Agent, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI, Muse Code and five open-source coding agents on your own model backends. For each question, the lead agent designs the team: each member’s role and model, and how they take turns. Once you confirm it, the real agents on your machine work on your code, or any question, and answer each other.

It also supports voice input, notification, branching in conversation, task scheduling, and mobile app(PWA) support!

If you are interested in this project, please give it a try and star us on the GitHub repo, thanks!

GitHub repo: https://github.com/Agentic-System-Lab/harness-relay

story_text.value:
Site URL: https://fmrl.live

Repository URL: https://gitlab.com/croatoa/fmrl

This project allows you to host a website, content, and streaming from an open browser window. It gets served over WebRTC connections (or a Cloudfare turn server if that's not available).

This is just a start. Any suggestions or feedback to improve usability, feature requests, etc is super welcome.

This is a project I've had in mind for a while. I wanted to participate in building for a decentralized web, so I thought it would be cool if people could run a social network kind of page from their own machine, and allow them to diffuse content over a peer to peer net, independent of the typical social media giants.

While this iteration is not quite that, it's a start.

While the UI probably makes this super obvious, this is the first time I've used AI in coding (LLM, Claude Code). It really is some impressive machinery.

The goal isn't privacy, but rather autonomy, more or less. I know there are real limitations (like a host user closing their browser) but I feel like the idea is at least slightly novel (probably because its a mediocre idea lol).. but it'll be interesting to see how it evolves.

If you made it this far, thanks for the read. Hope you have a pleasant day.

story_text.value:
Hi HN, this is Max, Marc and Clemens, co-founders of Langfuse, the open source tool for agent & observability & evals (https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse).

It’s been a minute since our last Show HN in August 2023 (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=37310070) - we’ve been busy building out and serving our tracing & eval pieces over the past years and have been very lucky to build a successful company and open source project around it. Today, we are happy to show the beta of Langfuse AI Gateway: https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/tree/main/ai-gateway. You may ask, why an AI Gateway as our second product: it’s been one our community’s strongest asks + integration pattern that we’ve seen. We want to offer a scalable, reliable and secure way to solve for the gateway use case in the same way that we’ve done with tracing/evals over the past years. And we’ve recently grown our team with some excellent folks - expect to see more bigger bets from us.

Our observability SDKs currently see the code you instrument. Much of a company's model traffic runs through code that is not or cannot be easily instrumented: coding agents like Pi, Claude Code and Codex, internal tools, scripts etc. Third party gateways are already popular ways to emit traces to Langfuse and we’re happy to now ship one natively.

You change your base URL and your API key. Langfuse AI Gateway forwards the native request with a provider key that does not need to be distributed across the team. Right now, it doesn't translate between APIs, responses are relayed unchanged. This was a conscious decision to ensure stability for gateway users, as translation between e.g. OpenAI responses and Anthropic messages are imperfect and might lead to subtle failures in your agents.

If you pass a traceparent header, the call lands inside your existing Langfuse traces.

You can try by docker composing langfuse up and then on to http://localhost:3000

--

git clone https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse.git

cd langfuse

docker compose up

--

On Cloud, each call becomes a Langfuse generation with tokens, cost, latency and time to first token. Prompts and outputs are recorded if you opt in. If you self-hosted you can also track nothing, not even metadata.

Some details:

- Written in Rust. Stateless, with no database; it talks only to the Langfuse platform and the providers.

- 22MB Docker image. Under 3ms median overhead with tracing on, 1,000+ concurrent streams on 2 vCPUs.

- MIT licensed. Self-host it with Docker Compose or Helm or use our Cloud version.

- Your provider keys and contracts. We don't resell tokens.

What’s next? - Budget caps per key, user, team

- Custom model aliases and fallbacks

- Guardrails

- PII redaction

- SCIM user provisioning

We’ll be around & looking forward to all questions & comments

title.value: Show HN: Langfuse AI Gateway, open source rust gateway to trace every LLM call

story_text.value:
Hello HN!

I've spent the last few months building solutions for friends and small businesses and creating mobile applications using Claude Code and Codex. Didn't get as much traction as I would have hoped for.

Last week I spent a bit more time on running models locally on my iPhone. I wanted to see what you can get done on a model with < 4B parameters and also keep my conversation private. My initial stab at it is JackAI.

It is an AI assistant leveraging local models. It supports Apple Foundation models as well as open-weight models like Qwen 3.5 2B, Gemma 4 E2B, Whisper, etc. You can use it to chat with files, live transcription, live translation, OCR, text summarization and even deterministic actions like generating a QR code.

It is available for free in the Apple App store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/jackai-offline-ai-assistant/id...

If you have a few minutes to download it and try it out, it would be appreciated. I'm looking for feedback and impressions.

Let me know what you think!

title.value: Show HN: JackAI Experimenting Local Models on iPhone
